items.title: Tropical Rainforest
items.notes: hot, high rainfall year-round, dense canopy layers (Amazon, Congo Basin, Southeast Asia)

items.notes: wet/dry seasons (parts of India, Southeast Asia)

items.title: Temperate Deciduous Forest
items.notes: four seasons, trees shed leaves (Eastern US, Europe, East Asia)

items.title: Temperate Rainforest
items.notes: cool, very high rainfall (Pacific Northwest, New Zealand, southern Chile)

items.title: Taiga / Boreal Forest
items.notes: cold, coniferous, world's largest land biome (Siberia, Canada, Scandinavia)

items.title: Mediterranean Forest / Woodland (Chaparral)
items.notes: hot dry summers, mild wet winters (California, Mediterranean Basin, parts of Australia/Chile)

items.title: Tropical Savanna
items.notes: warm year-round, wet/dry seasons, scattered trees (African Serengeti, parts of Australia/Brazil)

items.title: Temperate Grassland / Steppe / Prairie
items.notes: hot summers, cold winters, few trees (Great Plains, Eurasian Steppe, Pampas)

items.title: Hot Desert
items.notes: extreme heat, very low rainfall (Sahara, Arabian, Sonoran)

items.title: Cold Desert
items.notes: low rainfall, cold temperatures (Gobi, parts of Antarctica, Great Basin)

items.title: Semi-Arid Desert
items.notes: slightly more rainfall than hot deserts (parts of the American Southwest)

items.title: Coastal Desert
items.notes: fog-influenced, mild temps (Atacama, Namib)

items.title: Arctic Tundra
items.notes: permafrost, extremely cold, low vegetation (northern Canada, Siberia, Alaska)

items.title: Alpine Tundra
items.notes: high-altitude, similar cold conditions at elevation instead of latitude (Andes, Himalayas, Rockies)

items.title: Wetlands (freshwater)
